terms.definitionEn: A declaration that tells browsers to use modern HTML parsing mode.
terms.definitionAr: سطر في بداية الملف بيخلّي المتصفح يعرض الصفحة بوضع HTML الحديث.

terms.definitionEn: The root element that contains the complete page document.
terms.definitionAr: العنصر الأساسي اللي بيحتوي كل عناصر مستند الصفحة.

terms.definitionEn: The element containing document metadata and linked resources rather than page content.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر بيضم بيانات الصفحة وملفاتها المرتبطة، مش المحتوى الرئيسي الظاهر.

terms.definitionEn: The element containing the document content presented in the page.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر بيضم المحتوى اللي بيتعرض جوه الصفحة.

terms.definitionEn: An element that names the document in browser tabs and other browser interfaces.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر بيحدد اسم الصفحة اللي بيظهر في لسان المتصفح وواجهاته.

terms.definitionEn: An element that supplies descriptive information about a document through attributes.
terms.definitionAr: عنصر بيضيف معلومات وصفية عن الصفحة باستخدام خصائصه.

terms.definitionEn: An attribute that declares the character encoding used by a document.
terms.definitionAr: خاصية بتحدد ترميز الحروف اللي المتصفح يستخدمه لقراءة الصفحة.

terms.definitionEn: A metadata setting that controls the layout area on mobile devices.
terms.definitionAr: إعداد للـ metadata بيتحكم في مساحة عرض الصفحة على الموبايل.

terms.definitionEn: An attribute that identifies the primary tongue used by an element's text.
terms.definitionAr: خاصية بتحدد اللغة الأساسية للنص داخل العنصر.

terms.definitionEn: Information describing a document that is not usually displayed as page content.
terms.definitionAr: معلومات بتوصف المستند لكنها غالبًا مش جزء من محتوى الصفحة الظاهر.

terms.definitionEn: The single top-level element that contains the other elements in a document tree.
terms.definitionAr: العنصر الوحيد في أعلى شجرة الصفحة وبيحتوي باقي العناصر.

terms.definitionEn: A legacy browser rendering mode that may be selected when a document lacks the modern doctype.
terms.definitionAr: وضع توافق قديم ممكن المتصفح يختاره لو إعلان نوع المستند الحديث مش موجود.

questions.question: What does this declaration tell a modern browser?
options: Use the modern HTML parsing mode
Load the page as an XML document
Choose the page's visual theme
Treat the next element as hidden
questions.explanation: The HTML doctype selects standards mode; it is a declaration, not a content element.
questions.explanationAr: إعلان doctype بيختار وضع المعايير الحديث، ومش عنصر محتوى.

questions.question: Which element is the root containing both head and body?

The html element
The body element
The title element
questions.explanation: The html element is the document root and contains head and body.
questions.explanationAr: عنصر html هو جذر المستند وبيحتوي head وbody.

questions.question: Why is UTF-8 commonly declared near the start of head?
options: It converts every page string into an image
It determines how character bytes and CSS styling are interpreted
It makes all text use the same font size
It lets the browser decode a broad set of characters consistently
questions.explanation: Declaring the encoding early helps the browser interpret document bytes as the intended characters.
questions.explanationAr: إعلان الترميز بدري بيساعد المتصفح يقرأ الحروف بشكل صحيح.

questions.question: What changes when the modern doctype is omitted from this document?
options: The browser may use legacy quirks mode instead of standards mode
The browser automatically adds a viewport declaration
The title becomes visible inside the main element
The browser parses everything as legacy XML and ignores normal document structure
questions.explanation: Without the modern doctype, browsers may select quirks mode for legacy layout compatibility.
questions.explanationAr: من غير doctype الحديث، المتصفح ممكن يستخدم quirks mode للتوافق القديم.

questions.prompt: Complete the root-language declaration and place the title in document metadata.
questions.explanation: The html root owns the language setting and contains the separate head and body regions.

questions.question: Which text is page content rather than head metadata?
options: River survey, because title is always displayed in the body
Results, because it is inside the body heading
Water samples, because meta content is a visible paragraph
All three strings are rendered as body text
questions.explanation: The h1 is body content; title and meta description are document metadata.
questions.explanationAr: عنصر h1 محتوى داخل body، أما title والوصف فبيانات وصفية.

questions.prompt: Use the encoding declaration that supports Arabic and many other writing systems.
questions.explanation: UTF-8 can encode the characters used by Arabic and a wide range of other scripts.

questions.question: How do the responsibilities of html, head, and body differ in an HTML document?
keyPoints: head contains metadata and resource references
The document has one main head and body region
questions.modelAnswer: The html element is the root of the document tree. Its head contains metadata and resource links, while its body contains the content presented as the page.

questions.question: What does the HTML doctype do, and is it an HTML element?
keyPoints: It is a declaration at the document start
It selects standards mode in modern browsers
It is not a content element
It does not create visible page text
questions.modelAnswer: The HTML doctype tells the browser to use modern standards-mode parsing. It is a declaration rather than an element, so it does not add visible content to the page.

questions.question: Why should a page declare its character encoding early?
keyPoints: The browser must decode document bytes
UTF-8 supports many languages and symbols
Encoding is separate from visual styling
questions.modelAnswer: A browser needs to know how to decode the bytes in an HTML document into characters. Declaring UTF-8 near the beginning helps multilingual text display as intended and is unrelated to visual styling.

questions.question: What information does a viewport meta setting provide to mobile browsers?
keyPoints: device-width matches the device's CSS width
It does not replace responsive CSS
questions.modelAnswer: The viewport metadata can tell a mobile browser to size the layout viewport to the device width and choose an initial scale. Responsive CSS is still needed to adapt the layout itself.
